# Researching and ingesting wiki evidence

Choose the mode explicitly from the request. An unspecified request to use this
role is not permission to process the whole backlog; clarify the intended task.
Treat `` as the request when the host has not substituted it.

- **Discover sources on a topic:** read [discovery](references/discover.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md),
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md), and
  [efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md). Research perspectives
  return candidates without writing. Use the capture route only within the
  requested scope; a request for candidates alone remains read-only.
- **Capture named URLs or saved web pages:** read [named capture](references/capture.md)
  and [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md). Skip broad topic research;
  preserve deduplication, declines and capture checks.
- **Capture a named format or service:** read its complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or
  [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md). These routes include prerequisite
  checks; missing converters or authentication never justify fabricated evidence.
- **Ingest named existing clippings:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), and
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md). Use the exact source set;
  do not rediscover it or silently expand to the global backlog.
- **Process new or un-ingested clippings without a filename:** read
  [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join backlog contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Determine eligibility before writing. Preserve already summarized sources and
  reject restricted evidence as support. If nothing eligible is pending, report
  that without opening an operation, logging, committing or refreshing indexes.

Capture-only requests create evidence, never derived source or concept pages.
Ingestion needs authorization for that source set; an explicitly requested full
research-and-ingest flow already provides it. Only capture tools write raw
artifacts, and agents never edit their bodies. Read
[evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before assessing fidelity,
quoting or synthesizing; preserve restrictions and platform-specific sections.

Before the first authorized mutation, read
[operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md). Finish the
scoped validation, log, commit, sync and remote verification unless publication
is held. Reuse an enclosing operation when it owns the work; preserve other
writers' edits. For concept reuse and relationship changes read
[efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).

1	Read [access and host commands](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md) before touching the vault. Also read for this operation: [operations](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md).
2	Load the rest only when this run reaches it — [evidence](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before a quote or figure from this capture lands on a wiki page, or when reporting a fidelity limit.
3	Before the first authorized write, follow the shared operations completion contract; reuse existing session authorization.
4	
5	# Clipping a Confluence page into the wiki
6	
7	The HTML clipper (`clip.mjs` → Defuddle) handles public **HTML** pages
8	only, by an unauthenticated fetch. A Confluence Cloud page is also HTML, but
9	sits behind Atlassian auth — Defuddle's anonymous request hits the login wall
10	or an empty SPA shell, reads as thin content, and gets auto-declined. This
11	skill is the Confluence path. **The canonical stored artifact is the Markdown
12	the `confluence` skill's `page.mjs` already returns, never a PDF export and
13	never a second fetch** — that keeps the vault greppable, diffable, and
14	answerable, and makes `[[note]]` provenance resolve to a real clipping.
15	
16	**Why not export the page to PDF and run PDF capture on it instead?** That was
17	considered and rejected: it is a double lossy conversion (Confluence storage
18	format → PDF render → `pdftotext` extraction) instead of the one clean hop
19	`page.mjs` already does to Markdown, `clip-pdf.mjs`'s own code documents that
20	table extraction can "mispair rows beyond recovery" while looking perfectly
21	clean character-wise, and Confluence validation/compliance corpora are
22	dominated by exactly that shape of content (approval blocks, signature tables,
23	requirement-to-test traceability matrices). It also does not fix live Jira
24	macros that already fail to render for `page.mjs` ("Data cannot be retrieved
25	due to an unexpected error") — that is a server-side macro-render failure,
26	likely reproduced in PDF export too, minus the helpful fallback JQL link
27	`page.mjs` gives you. And it stays fully manual per page, which does not scale
28	to a researcher discovery-style sweep across dozens of pages.
29	
30	## How it works
31	
32	`clip-confluence.mjs` does **not** implement its own Confluence client. It
33	shells out to the **separately installed** `confluencer` plugin's own
34	`page.mjs` (the same script the `confluence` skill uses), parses the
35	provenance header `page.mjs` always prints (`# Title` / `Space: X · Page ID: Y
36	· Version: Z · Updated: <iso>` / `URL: <url>` / `---` / body), and writes
37	`raw/clippings/<slug>.md` with the standard clipping frontmatter (`source`,
38	`created`, `tags:[clippings]`, `quality`, `source-hash`) — the Confluence-
39	specific detail (space, page ID, version, updated timestamp) stays in the
40	clipping's body exactly as `page.mjs` formatted it, rather than growing the
41	shared frontmatter schema for one source type. It skips duplicates and prior
42	declines, and records a decline for a **thin** extraction (a parent/index page
43	with no body prose) so it is not retried blindly.
44	
45	**Deliberate exception to wiki-master's usual portability rule.** Every other
46	`clip-*` skill (pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx) is self-contained — none of them
47	runtime-depend on another installed Copilot plugin, specifically so wiki-master
48	behaves the same whether or not some other plugin happens to be present. This
49	skill breaks that rule on purpose: Confluence access is a whole configured,
50	authenticated Atlassian integration (base URL, account email, API token,
51	connectivity), not a generic stateless library like `pandoc` or `python-pptx`,
52	and re-implementing an Atlassian API client inside wiki-master to preserve
53	portability would be the wrong trade. So this capture route treats `confluencer` as an
54	**optional** runtime dependency and is built to degrade gracefully rather than
55	fail confusingly when it is absent — see the next section.
56	
57	## Graceful degradation when confluencer isn't installed
58	
59	`clip-confluence.mjs` never assumes `confluencer` is present. It searches
60	every `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/*/confluencer/` install for its `page.mjs`
61	under that plugin's own `scripts` folder (every Copilot CLI plugin installs
62	under that root, even though neither plugin knows the
63	other's exact path at authoring time), or an explicit
64	`WIKI_MASTER_CONFLUENCER_SCRIPTS` env var override for a dev checkout or
65	non-standard install.
66	
67	- **Preflight, any time:** `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-confluence.mjs" --doctor`
68	  reports whether `confluencer` was found, and if so, hands off to **its own**
69	  `doctor.mjs` for the auth/config/connectivity check — wiki-master has no
70	  business diagnosing another plugin's credentials, only routing to the tool
71	  that can.
72	- **Not found:** the clip attempt prints one clear message (which paths it
73	  searched, and the env var that can override) and returns
74	  `{ status: 'confluencer-missing' }` — never a raw `ENOENT`/stack trace, and
75	  never a fabricated clipping standing in for content nobody actually fetched.
76	- **Found but failing** (bad page ID, expired token, network): the real
77	  `page.mjs` stderr is surfaced (first few lines) plus a pointer to run
78	  confluencer's own `doctor.mjs`.
79	
80	If it reports missing, either install the `confluencer` plugin, or hand-fetch
81	the page via the `confluence` skill yourself and clip it through Word capture
82	or PDF capture as a fallback (lower fidelity for tables, per the rejected-PDF
83	argument above, but better than nothing) — do not hand-write a
84	`raw/clippings/*.md` file directly; that would bypass dedup, decline-tracking,
85	and hashing the same way it would for any other source type.
86	
87	## Steps
88	
89	1. **Preflight** (once, or whenever a clip fails unexpectedly):
90	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-confluence.mjs" --doctor`.
91	2. **Clip** (this is the only writer to `raw/` for Confluence pages):
92	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-confluence.mjs" "<url-or-page-id>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>"`
93	   - Accepts anything `page.mjs` itself accepts as a positional argument: a
94	     canonical URL, a tiny link (`/wiki/x/…`), a legacy `viewpage.action` URL,
95	     or a bare numeric page ID. If you only have an exact title + space, first
96	     resolve it via the `confluence` skill (`page.mjs --title "..." --space
97	     ...` or `search.mjs`), then pass the resulting URL/ID here.
98	   - No `--source=` flag (unlike `clip-pdf`/`clip-docx`) — the canonical URL
99	     always comes from `page.mjs`'s own metadata, which is the authoritative
100	     citation per the `confluence` skill's own rule ("always cite the title,
101	     URL, and version").
102	   - **`--topic` whenever this clip belongs to a research run** — pass the
103	     topic string researcher discovery was given, identical across every clip in
104	     the run, so maintainer triage can group the run's leftovers together.
105	     **Topic is recorded going forward only and no tool can retro-fit it**, so
106	     a clip made without it is an *Unattributed* triage row permanently. Omit
107	     it only when there is no research run behind the clip; never invent one.
108	   - A `thin` result means the page has no readable body (a parent/index page
109	     with only child links) — a decline is recorded; this is not a failure.
110	   - A `failed` result means `page.mjs` itself errored (bad id/auth/network) —
111	     report it for manual handling; do not invent the text.
112	3. **Verify** the clipping landed: read `raw/clippings/<slug>.md` and
113	   sanity-check the body against what `page.mjs` would show you directly via
114	   the `confluence` skill.
115	4. **Only when ingestion is authorized, follow [ingestion](ingest.md)** for this exact clipping —
116	   summarize into `wiki/sources/`, cross-reference, index, log. Ingestion requires authorization for this scope; reuse explicit session authorization.
117	
118	## Known limitation: re-clipping an updated page
119	
120	Confluence pages mutate in place at a stable URL — a page's `Version` can
121	climb many times in a single day. The dedup gate is keyed on bare URL (same as
122	every other `clip-*` script), so deliberately re-clipping a page that has been
123	edited since its last clip reads as `duplicate (already clipped)` and is
124	silently skipped, exactly as it would for any live web page whose content
125	changed since its last clip. This is not new to Confluence, but Confluence
126	pages hit it far more often than the mostly-static sources the dedup layer was
127	designed around. Not fixed here — flagged for a future version-aware dedup
128	(key on URL **+ Version**, not URL alone) if re-clipping updated pages becomes
129	a real workflow.
130	
131	## Guardrails
132	
133	- **Never edit the body of anything under `raw/`** — clipped content is
134	  immutable source-of-truth (guardrail #1). Frontmatter is pipeline state,
135	  tooling-only.
136	- `clip-confluence.mjs` is the **sole writer** to `raw/` for Confluence pages —
137	  the model never writes the clipping by hand (that would bypass dedup,
138	  decline, and hashing).
139	- **Fidelity, not truth**: a faithful clip of a wrong or outdated page is still
140	  wrong — confirm you clipped the page you meant, and note the `Version` you
141	  clipped when citing it, since the live page may have moved on.
142	
143	## Completion
144	
145	For a standalone clip, open an operation before the clipping helper writes, verify
146	its returned paths and extraction diagnostics, log once, commit, push and verify
147	remote publication through the shared operations contract. During discovery,
148	use the enclosing operation and report the results to its owner for completion.
149	Pass `--since <saved-token>` to the clipping helper so every written path enters
150	that operation's ledger. Capture-only requests end after this completion and
151	create no derived source or concept pages.
152	Capturing evidence does not by itself authorize ingestion; reuse explicit
153	discover-and-ingest authorization when it is already present.

every `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/*/confluencer/` install for its `page.mjs`
under that plugin's own `scripts` folder (every Copilot CLI plugin installs
under that root, even though neither plugin knows the
other's exact path at authoring time), or an explicit

- **Preflight, any time:** `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-confluence.mjs" --doctor`

1. **Preflight** (once, or whenever a clip fails unexpectedly):
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-confluence.mjs" --doctor`.
2. **Clip** (this is the only writer to `raw/` for Confluence pages):
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-confluence.mjs" "<url-or-page-id>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>"`
   - Accepts anything `page.mjs` itself accepts as a positional argument: a
     canonical URL, a tiny link (`/wiki/x/…`), a legacy `viewpage.action` URL,
     or a bare numeric page ID. If you only have an exact title + space, first
     resolve it via the `confluence` skill (`page.mjs --title "..." --space

climb many times in a single day. The dedup gate is keyed on bare URL (same as

**Routing result**

- **Skill invoked:** `wiki-master:wiki-researcher`. The request asks to capture an authenticated Confluence page as evidence, which is this skill's job. wiki-user, wiki-maintainer, wiki-init and wiki-purge don't fit.
- **Mode:** capture a named format or service, using the Confluence route. This is a single named URL, so it is not topic discovery, not ingestion and not a backlog run.
- **Loaded references:** only `skills/wiki-researcher/references/clip-confluence.md`. That was enough to identify the mode. I did not read the access, operations or evidence references it points to, because those apply only when the workflow actually runs.

**What the route would do, if it were run**
1. Read the access and operations references.
2. Run `clip-confluence.mjs --doctor`. This checks that the separately installed `confluencer` plugin exists and is authenticated.
3. Run `clip-confluence.mjs "<url>" --quality=<tier>`. This is the only writer to `raw/clippings/`. I'd add `--topic` only if the capture belongs to a research run, and `--since <token>` so the written paths enter the operation's ledger.
4. Check the resulting clipping.
5. Finish the operation: log, commit, push and verify the remote.

**Scope and approval boundaries**
- This is capture-only. It creates a raw clipping and no derived source or concept pages. Ingestion would need separate explicit authorization, which the request doesn't give.
- If `confluencer` is missing, the route returns `confluencer-missing`. If `page.mjs` fails, it returns `failed`. In both cases nothing is fabricated and no clipping is written by hand. A page with no readable body is declined as `thin`.
- A page that was already clipped is skipped as a duplicate, even if it has been edited since.
- The clip should record which `Version` was captured, because the live page may have moved on.
- Publishing (commit, push, remote verification) is part of the operation unless you hold it.
- **Clarification:** the wiki root is not specified. I'd confirm which vault to write to before any real run.
- For this probe I ran no commands, made no captures and touched no vault.
